title: Wu experiment: nature tells left from right
place: National Bureau of Standards, Washington, D.C., USA
summary: Chien-Shiung Wu led the experiment showing that parity is not conserved in weak nuclear decays, overturning an assumed symmetry of physics.
why: Proved that nature's laws are not mirror-symmetric.

notes.problem: The 1956 experiment ran at the NBS low-temperature laboratory in Washington DC: Wu experiment page caption 'performed at the Bureau of Standards low temperature laboratory, Washington DC, in 1956'. The biography's 'Maryland' conflicts with it.

unsung.contribution: Designed and led the experiment proving that parity is not conserved in weak interactions.
unsung.recognition: Theorists Lee and Yang won the 1957 Nobel Prize for the discovery; Wu was not included.
